newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada unemployment falls to 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada unemployment falls to 9.7 pct.

text.p: Following are reactions to unemployment data released by Statistics Canada on Friday.
Statistics Canada said the unemployment rate fell to 9.7 percent in December from 10.0 percent in November.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, a fall to 9.84 percent.
Mark Mullins, chief economist, Midland Walwyn Capital Inc - "It's a good number. It looks like it's full-time gains and you have a confirmation here from the help wanted index a couple of days ago.
"That (help wanted) number was very strong and it tends to lead by a few months so we are likely to see these kinds of numbers continuing."
Doug Porter, senior economist, Nesbitt Burns Inc -- "I would say most people had pretty strong expectations for these numbers and they were pretty close to expectations.
"If anything, we were maybe looking for a touch stronger (employment gain) given the indicators we have seen so far from November and December.
Porter -- "I believe this is really just the beginning of a trend we are going to see throughout this year. I believe we are going to see the jobless rate fall pretty quickly in 1997.
Michael Gregory, economist, Lehman Brothers -- "It's good news. The economy is continuing to expand, not at a booming pace but enough to instill a rising consumer confidence.

"Finally, the economy has sort of shaken off the shackles of poor economic growth. But I think the result of this is that the Bank of Canada will shift to a neutral stance. I think the days of easing are over."
